title: Config: set up once
lede: What has to exist before the demo runs: the PingOne apps and flow, the gateway, the Muse pod, and the connector in Meta’s Muse. Arrows are the setup, in order.

lanes.label: PingOne: who signs in, and how an agent is recognised
Agent Privilege and Agent Gateway: what the agent may reach
Muse (hosted on the US SE cluster)
Meta's Muse: adding the Airline Connector

nodes.label: Muse agent login (app)
sub: confidential: auth code + PKCE, token exchange, client credentials

nodes.label: Muse user login (app)
sub: public: auth code + PKCE. Not the Muse app, so never flagged as an agent

nodes.label: Muse Login (DaVinci flow policy)
sub: assigned to both apps. Branches on the app id

nodes.label: Protect predictor museAgentClient
sub: Muse app id = HIGH, in the default risk policy set

nodes.label: Muse Privilege MCP (resource)
sub: puts protect_agent = HIGH into the token

nodes.label: Agreements
sub: Muse Consent, and Airline Connector Consent

nodes.label: MFA policy
sub: required on medium risk; login hint .nomfa turns it off for the demo

nodes.label: P1 Privilege Agent App
sub: fronts the gateway and passes the token through

nodes.label: Agent Gateway
sub: checks signature, audience and scope; 401 with metadata when no token

nodes.label: PingOne Authorize
sub: allows only: right audience, Muse as actor, this tool

nodes.label: Secret muse-real
sub: tenant ids, client secret, airline name, user app id. Written by the owner script

nodes.label: Muse pod
sub: UI, /api, and the Airline Connector at /mcp

steps.title: Protect rule
steps.what: A Protect predictor recognises the Muse app id and rates it HIGH.
steps.why: Sign-in learns an agent is asking without trusting the agent to say so.

steps.title: Consent screens
steps.what: Two agreements exist: Muse Consent and Airline Connector Consent.
steps.why: Sam sees consent that names who is acting.

steps.title: Flow on Muse app
steps.what: The Muse Login flow policy is assigned to the Muse agent login app.
steps.why: Sign-ins from Muse show the agent screen and ask for consent.

steps.title: Flow on user app
steps.what: The same flow policy is assigned to Muse user login.
steps.why: The flow compares the app id, so this app skips the agent screen and consent.

steps.title: protect_agent claim
steps.what: The Muse Privilege MCP resource copies protect_agent from the user into the token.
steps.why: The Muse page can show Protect’s verdict, red or blue.

steps.title: Fronts the gateway
steps.what: The P1 Privilege Agent App fronts Agent Gateway and passes the token through.
steps.why: Agents reach the tools only through it.

steps.title: Asks Authorize
steps.what: Agent Gateway asks PingOne Authorize before each tool call.
steps.why: Audience, actor and tool are checked. Sam’s own token has no actor.

steps.title: Secret to env
steps.what: The muse-real Secret holds tenant ids, the client secret, the airline name and the user app id. The pod reads it as environment.
steps.why: No credential lives in the repo.

steps.title: Ingress to pod
steps.what: Ingress and the certificate send {{origin}} to the pod.
steps.why: One public host serves the UI, the API and the connector.

steps.title: Pod signs in
steps.what: Muse redirects Sam to PingOne using the Muse agent login app.

steps.title: Pod calls gateway
steps.what: With the delegated token the pod calls the P1 Privilege Agent App.
steps.why: It is the only route to the tools.

steps.title: Add connector
steps.what: In Meta’s Muse, add a custom connector.
steps.why: Meta’s Muse then treats Muse as one more tool server.

steps.title: Client ID
steps.what: Enter client id airline-connector and leave the client secret blank.
steps.why: Meta’s Muse is a public client; PKCE protects the code.

steps.title: Callback host
steps.what: Meta’s callback is agent.meta.ai/api/hatch/oauth/callback. Muse allows only that host.
steps.why: Codes go only to a host the owner approved.

steps.title: Reaches /mcp
steps.what: The server URL points at the Muse pod’s /mcp endpoint.
steps.why: That endpoint answers 401 and tells Meta’s Muse where to sign in.
